content.text:
`MedianOfThreePivotSelector` works by treating the three indices as local variables and running a 3-element insertion sort on them — three comparisons, two possible swaps of index labels (not array contents). After those three steps the invariant `arr[low] ≤ arr[mid] ≤ arr[high]` holds for the local copies, so `mid` is the median index. The array itself is never touched here; the actual element swap happens in `partition` as usual.

Why this matters: on already-sorted or reverse-sorted input, `lastPivot` consistently picks the min or max, producing O(n²) partitions. Median-of-three picks the middle-valued element, yielding much more balanced splits without the randomness dependency of `randomPivot`.
